name: Blue Lagoon & the Reykjanes Peninsula
tagline: Iceland's most famous geothermal spa, surrounded by a raw volcanic peninsula that has been actively rearranging itself since 2021.
highlight: Sinking shoulder-deep into the Blue Lagoon's warm, milky-blue water with a silica mask on, steam rising into cold air around you.
shortDescription: A world-famous geothermal spa on Iceland's volcanic front doorstep, surrounded by lava fields, hot springs and a lighthouse at the edge of the sea.
metaDescription: A Blue Lagoon and Reykjanes Peninsula travel guide: the geothermal spa, Gunnuhver, the Bridge Between Two Continents and how to plan a visit near Keflavík airport.
nearestAirport: Keflavík International (KEF) — genuinely on the peninsula itself
knownFor: The Blue Lagoon, geothermal fields, recent volcanic activity
budget: ISK 15,000–35,000 per day, depending on spa package
goodFor: Arrival or departure day, geothermal spas, geology

intro: The Reykjanes Peninsula is genuinely where most visitors' trip to Iceland actually begins and ends, since Keflavík International Airport sits right on it — and it happens to also hold the country's single most famous attraction, the Blue Lagoon, a milky-blue geothermal spa fed by a nearby power plant.

Beyond the lagoon, Reykjanes is genuinely one of the most volcanically active places in Iceland: a series of eruptions near Fagradalsfjall and Sundhnúkagígar since 2021 has put this peninsula on the news repeatedly, and its stark lava fields, steaming vents and bubbling mudpots make that activity easy to see firsthand.

It's a genuinely compact place — small enough to fold into a single half-day between a flight and a hotel check-in, but rewarding enough that some travellers give it a full day of its own, mixing the spa with the raw geothermal and volcanic landscape around it.

whyVisit.intro: The Reykjanes Peninsula's case rests on convenience and raw geology in roughly equal measure.

points.title: The Blue Lagoon is genuinely one of the most photographed spas on Earth
points.text: A milky-blue geothermal lagoon with an in-water bar, silica mud masks and views out over black lava fields.

points.title: It's genuinely the easiest big Icelandic sight to combine with a flight
points.text: Minutes from Keflavík airport, making it a natural first or last stop for almost every visitor.

points.title: The peninsula is genuinely one of Iceland's most volcanically active zones right now
points.text: Repeated eruptions since 2021 have reshaped parts of the landscape within living memory.

points.title: It's genuinely rich in geothermal features beyond the lagoon
points.text: Gunnuhver's steaming mudpots and the Krýsuvík-Seltún field are both dramatic, uncrowded alternatives.

points.title: The Bridge Between Two Continents is a genuinely rare novelty
points.text: One of very few places on Earth where you can walk directly over the boundary between two tectonic plates.

attractionsIntro: Reykjanes packs a genuinely striking range of geothermal and volcanic sights into a small, easily looped area.

attractions.name: The Blue Lagoon

image.alt: Bathers in the milky-blue water of the Blue Lagoon geothermal spa

attractions.text: Iceland's genuinely most famous single attraction, a warm, silica-rich lagoon fed by the adjacent Svartsengi geothermal plant, ringed by black lava rock.
attractions.tip: Book your entry slot genuinely well ahead — it sells out, especially around flight times.

attractions.name: Gunnuhver Hot Springs

image.alt: Steaming mudpots and vents at the Gunnuhver geothermal area

attractions.text: Iceland's genuinely largest mudpot, named for a vengeful ghost local legend says was lured into it, surrounded by hissing steam vents on a boardwalk trail.
attractions.tip: Stay genuinely on the boardwalk — the ground nearby is unstable and dangerously hot.

attractions.name: Reykjanesviti Lighthouse

image.alt: Reykjanesviti, Iceland's oldest lighthouse, on a coastal hill

attractions.text: Iceland's genuinely oldest lighthouse, standing on a hill above dramatic sea cliffs at the peninsula's windswept southwestern tip.
attractions.tip: The surrounding cliffs are genuinely worth a short walk beyond the lighthouse itself for the coastal views.

attractions.name: Bridge Between Two Continents

image.alt: A small footbridge over a rift symbolising the border of two tectonic plates

attractions.text: A genuinely symbolic footbridge over a narrow rift, marketed as spanning the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates.
attractions.tip: It's a genuinely quick five-minute stop — worth it for the novelty rather than the scenery alone.

attractions.name: Krýsuvík-Seltún Geothermal Area

image.alt: Colourful mineral-stained ground and steam vents at the Seltún geothermal field

attractions.text: A genuinely vivid geothermal field of boiling mudpots and mineral-stained yellow and orange ground, far quieter than the Blue Lagoon.
attractions.tip: The boardwalk loop takes genuinely only 20-30 minutes and needs no special gear.

attractions.name: Lake Kleifarvatn

image.alt: Lake Kleifarvatn surrounded by dark volcanic hills

attractions.text: Iceland's genuinely largest lake on the peninsula, a stark, often mirror-calm body of water ringed by dark volcanic hills, with no streams feeding or draining it visibly.
attractions.tip: The roadside pull-offs along its shore are genuinely good, quiet spots for photos.

attractions.name: Valahnúkur Sea Cliffs

image.alt: Dramatic sea cliffs and black sand at Valahnúkur near Reykjanesviti

attractions.text: Genuinely dramatic basalt sea cliffs near the lighthouse, facing directly into the North Atlantic with crashing surf below.
attractions.tip: Keep genuinely well back from the cliff edge — the wind here can be strong and unpredictable.

thingsToDoIntro: Reykjanes rewards a mix of relaxing and exploring, since the spa and the raw landscape around it are such different experiences.

thingsToDo.title: Soak in the Blue Lagoon

image.alt: Sunrise light over the Blue Lagoon's geothermal water

thingsToDo.text: The genuinely signature Reykjanes experience — warm, mineral-rich water, a swim-up bar and a silica mask, all with a backdrop of black lava.
thingsToDo.tip: An early or late slot genuinely gives you softer light and a quieter lagoon.

thingsToDo.title: Stand on two tectonic plates at once

image.alt: The rift between two tectonic plates near the Bridge Between Two Continents

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely fun, quick novelty stop, walking the short bridge that symbolically links the North American and Eurasian plates.
thingsToDo.tip: Combine it genuinely with the nearby lighthouse and sea cliffs for one efficient stop.

thingsToDo.title: Watch Gunnuhver's mudpots steam

image.alt: Steam rising from Gunnuhver's boiling mudpots

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely visceral, sulphur-scented reminder of what powers the Blue Lagoon just down the road — boiling mud and roaring steam vents.
thingsToDo.tip: Midday light genuinely shows the steam plumes best against the sky.

thingsToDo.title: Hike the Reykjanesvegur trail past the lighthouse

image.file: File:Reykjanesviti, taken from the hiking trail Reykjavegur, Iceland 34.jpg
image.alt: The Reykjanesvegur hiking trail near Reykjanesviti lighthouse

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely rewarding stretch of Iceland's long-distance Reykjavegur trail, tracing the coast past the lighthouse and sea cliffs.
thingsToDo.tip: Even a genuinely short 20-30 minute stretch of the trail gives excellent coastal views.

thingsToDo.title: Explore the peninsula's fresh lava fields

image.alt: Weathered volcanic lava terrain on the Reykjanes Peninsula

thingsToDo.text: Much of the peninsula is genuinely raw, mossy or bare lava rock, some of it from eruptions within the last few years.
thingsToDo.tip: Stick genuinely to marked paths — recent lava fields can hide unstable ground.

thingsToDo.title: Spot seabirds at the sea cliffs

image.alt: Seabirds along the cliffs near Reykjanesviti

thingsToDo.text: The cliffs near Reykjanesviti genuinely host nesting seabirds in season, with the surf below adding real drama.
thingsToDo.tip: Binoculars genuinely help — the birds nest well down the cliff face.

foods.whereToTry: Supermarkets and cafés in Keflavík and Reykjanesbær.

foods.name: Icelandic hot dog

foods.text: A genuinely quick, cheap classic for a last meal before a flight or a first one off the plane.

foods.text: Iceland's genuinely famous caraway-flavoured schnapps, a fitting first or last drink of an Icelandic trip.

accommodation.intro: Most visitors genuinely stay near Reykjanes only on their arrival or departure night, given how close it sits to the airport.

areas.name: The Blue Lagoon's own hotels
areas.bestFor: A genuine splurge night bookending a flight
areas.text: The Retreat and Silica hotels offer genuinely direct or private lagoon access.

areas.name: Keflavík or Reykjanesbær
areas.text: Genuinely close to both the airport and the Blue Lagoon, with far lower rates.

areas.name: Reykjavik
areas.bestFor: Combining Reykjanes with a wider Iceland trip
areas.text: Genuinely only 45 minutes from the peninsula, and the standard base for most itineraries.

gettingThere.intro: Reykjanes is genuinely the first and last part of Iceland almost every visitor sees, given the airport's location.

options.text: The genuinely simplest option — the Blue Lagoon is about 20 minutes from Keflavík and 45 from Reykjavik.
options.detail: Route 41 and 43 connect the airport, the lagoon and Reykjavik directly.

options.text: Genuinely frequent shuttle buses run between Keflavík, the Blue Lagoon and Reykjavik.
options.detail: Many transfer companies allow a Blue Lagoon stopover built into the airport transfer.

options.text: Genuinely convenient if combining Reykjanes with the Golden Circle or South Coast in one day.
options.detail: Most tours run from Reykjavik with hotel pickup included.

gettingAround.intro: The peninsula's sights are genuinely spread along a couple of main roads, easy to link in one loop.

options.text: Genuinely the most flexible way to link the lagoon, Gunnuhver and the lighthouse in one trip.
options.detail: Roads 425 and 426 connect most of the peninsula's main sights.

options.text: Genuinely cover the main stops for visitors without a car, often bundled with an airport transfer.
options.detail: Half-day tours typically include the lagoon plus one or two other stops.

options.text: Genuinely all the peninsula's individual sights are short, well-marked walks from their car parks.
options.detail: None require more than 20-30 minutes on foot.

bestTime.headline: Any season — though check for volcanic activity advisories first
bestTime.summary: The Blue Lagoon genuinely operates year-round, and Reykjanes's paved roads stay open in most weather, but recent eruptions have periodically closed parts of the peninsula.

seasons.text: Long daylight and easy access, genuinely the most convenient season for combining stops.
Genuinely atmospheric for a lagoon soak, with a chance of the northern lights overhead.
Genuinely quieter, with mild weather still holding on most days.
Genuinely comfortable and increasingly bright as the days lengthen.

bestTime.avoid: Check genuinely current volcanic activity advisories before visiting — eruptions since 2021 have periodically closed roads and even the lagoon itself.

itinerary.intro: Built around a lagoon soak plus the peninsula's geothermal highlights, timed around a flight.

days.summary: The Blue Lagoon plus Reykjanes's raw geothermal landscape.
days.morning: Gunnuhver Hot Springs and the Bridge Between Two Continents.
days.afternoon: Reykjanesviti Lighthouse and the Valahnúkur sea cliffs.
days.evening: A relaxed soak at the Blue Lagoon before heading to the airport or Reykjavik.

tipsIntro: A handful of practical notes make a Reykjanes stop go far more smoothly.
tips: Book your Blue Lagoon entry slot genuinely well in advance — it regularly sells out.
Check for genuinely current volcanic activity or road closure advisories before setting out.
Store your bags genuinely at the lagoon's lockers if visiting straight off a flight.
Bring your own genuinely reusable water bottle — tap water across Iceland is excellent.
Pack flip-flops for the genuinely rough lava-rock ground around the lagoon's pool deck.
Allow a genuinely realistic 3-4 hours at the Blue Lagoon alone if you want the full spa experience.

faq.q: Is the Blue Lagoon worth it?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely, for most visitors — it's a relaxing, easy stop directly on the way to or from the airport, even if it is touristy.

faq.q: How far is the Blue Lagoon from Keflavík airport?
faq.a: About 20 minutes by car, genuinely making it one of the easiest big sights to fit around a flight.

faq.q: Do you need to book the Blue Lagoon in advance?
faq.a: Yes — entry is genuinely capped and slots regularly sell out, especially around midday and flight times.

faq.q: Is Reykjanes affected by volcanic eruptions?
faq.a: Yes — the peninsula has genuinely seen repeated eruptions since 2021, so it's worth checking current advisories before visiting.

faq.q: Can you visit Reykjanes without a car?
faq.a: Yes — shuttle buses and organised tours genuinely connect the airport, the Blue Lagoon and Reykjavik regularly.

faq.q: How much time do you need on the Reykjanes Peninsula?
faq.a: Half a day genuinely covers the Blue Lagoon plus one or two other stops; a full day allows the whole geothermal loop at an easy pace.
